blocks.text: Walk through a compound in Ibadan after the first rains and you will meet a moss cushion on a damp wall, a fern in the shade of a wall, a tall cypress by the gate and a hibiscus in flower. All four are plants, yet they belong to four different divisions, and one simple question separates them: how do they reproduce?

blocks.markdown:
## The plant kingdom in four divisions

The plant kingdom is divided according to whether the plant has proper transport vessels, and whether it makes spores or seeds.

**Bryophyta** (mosses and liverworts) have no vascular tissue and no true roots — only thread-like rhizoids. They are small, live in damp shaded places, and reproduce by spores. Water is essential for their sperm to swim to the egg.

**Pteridophyta** (ferns) have true roots, stems and leaves with xylem and phloem, so they grow larger, but they still reproduce by **spores** produced in sporangia on the underside of the fronds.

**Gymnospermophyta** (conifers such as cypress and pine) produce **naked seeds** in cones. There is no fruit, and the leaves are usually needle-like.

**Angiospermophyta** (flowering plants) produce seeds **enclosed in a fruit**, which develops from the ovary. This is the largest and most successful division and includes every crop grown in Nigeria.

### Monocots and dicots

Flowering plants split into two classes, and WAEC frequently asks you to tell them apart.

| Feature | Monocotyledon | Dicotyledon |
|---|---|---|
| Seed leaves | One | Two |
| Leaf venation | Parallel | Net-like (reticulate) |
| Root system | Fibrous | Taproot |
| Flower parts | In threes | In fours or fives |
| Examples | Maize, rice, guinea corn, palm | Cowpea, groundnut, mango, cassava |

blocks.title: Invertebrate and vertebrate
blocks.text: Invertebrates have no vertebral column (backbone) and make up over 95% of animal species. Vertebrates belong to the phylum Chordata and have an internal skeleton with a backbone enclosing the spinal cord.

blocks.title: Identifying an arthropod class
blocks.prompt: A student catches an animal with a hard external covering, a body divided into head, thorax and abdomen, three pairs of legs, two pairs of wings and one pair of antennae. Name its phylum and class, and give one reason for each.

steps.text: A hard external covering plus jointed legs places it in the phylum Arthropoda — these are the two defining arthropod features.
Count the legs. Three pairs (six legs) rules out Arachnida, which has four pairs, and Crustacea and Myriapoda, which have many more.
Check the body regions. Head, thorax and abdomen as three distinct regions is characteristic of the class Insecta; arachnids have only two regions.
Confirm with the antennae and wings. Insects have one pair of antennae and often two pairs of wings; arachnids have no antennae and no wings.

blocks.answer: Phylum Arthropoda, because it has jointed limbs and a chitinous exoskeleton; class Insecta, because it has three pairs of legs, three body regions, one pair of antennae and wings.

rows: Eggs laid in water; larval tadpole stage
Internal development; young fed on milk
blocks.caption: The five classes of vertebrates

blocks.title: Answer with the diagnostic feature
blocks.text: When a question asks why an organism belongs to a group, name the feature unique to that group. 'A bat is a mammal because it has hair and feeds its young on milk' scores; 'because it is an animal' does not. Note that a bat flies but is not a bird — feathers, not flight, define Aves.

points: Bryophytes lack vascular tissue; pteridophytes have it but still reproduce by spores.
Gymnosperms bear naked seeds in cones; angiosperms bear seeds enclosed in fruits.
Monocots have one seed leaf, parallel veins and fibrous roots; dicots have two seed leaves, net veins and a taproot.
Arthropods are recognised by jointed limbs and an exoskeleton; insects specifically have three pairs of legs and three body regions.
The five vertebrate classes are distinguished mainly by body covering, temperature control and mode of reproduction.
